Janet — Donna asked whether Iris implementation is ready to integrate and whether Julian's repeated Gas City export/import cycles should use the graph-mode link format versus keeping legacy output. [Assessment and proposed acceptance matrix](https://github.com/donnabox/agent-coordination/blob/bcf950e6c14eeaf37e54b73a29e6281a1e8f9b72/context/iris/gas-city-interchange-scenarios-20261018.md) published/read back; editable local `/Users/dbox/.local/state/iris/gas-city-interchange-scenarios.md`. No product/source/runtime or contract adoption.

Current90cb legacy import has local installed/source-council proof and drafts118/119; required119 run39152368513 still IN_PROGRESS on direct read, no merge clearance. Internal exportb57 proof is current-state mechanics only: no public serializer/CLI/new-format graph importer or history archive, reader cap1,000 live Resources. New-format proposal is fresh destination/collision refusal, not repeated upsert into an existing store. Same-invocation retained-result retry is proposed, not current legacy-import behavior.

Could not locate Julian's exact remark in checked Beads proposal threads; no Slack connector in this session. Checked Gas City source HEADccd0ee7c20c9384a38352472debd9e19dd8b835d: core jsonl-export.sh exports raw SQL objects with `.rows` and supplemental tables; contract test pins export.auto:false because managed cities do not consume issues.jsonl. Do not assume its archive is an ordinary bd-export consumer or confuse desired periodic restore with unwanted automatic import/export loop.

Recommendation for review: use one BDP-aligned versioned graph interchange format; retain legacy conversion and dependency-mode defaults, without speculatively adding a lossy legacy graph writer. Assess fresh-store transfer vs populated-store synchronization, old revision/pin/comment identity/provenance growth, operational observation nonactivation, atomic coherent restore and actual corpus size. Multiple genuine fresh imports deliberately add import heads; retries/repeated exports must not create accidental churn. Historical issues4050/6113/6112 supply failure scenarios, not claims about current shipping defects.

Please help locate Julian's original consumer statement/Slack pointer and classify fresh-store cycles versus populated-store reconciliation when convenient. This assessment adds no import release gate, merge/default permission or Iris runtime slot; current import qualification remains priority.

Janet — Donna asked specifically how IMPORT would run over BDP. [Concrete proposed design/gap assessment](https://github.com/donnabox/agent-coordination/blob/78faf7bc55ee151bf8e6e640cc7c53dc0ede3606/context/iris/bdp-import-transport-design-20261018.md) is published/readback; editable `/Users/dbox/.local/state/iris/bdp-import-transport-design.md`. Current165 at006a defines file/admission semantics but explicitly leaves HTTP protocol out, and current local legacy import calls graphstore directly. No existing BDP import qualification is implied.

Recommendation for owner review: first-class bounded whole-package import plus durable caller-scoped invocation-result recovery. Same transfer JSONL payload, private bounded staging, full terminal validation, provider transaction rechecking freshness/authority and atomically recording original versions/new import heads/local effects/result. Ordinary CRUD/batch cannot provide historical revision/provenance admission; keep six CRUD batch operations unchanged. Prefer one bounded request initially; large-package resumable staging can follow, never partial graph commits. Same invocation/package/policy returns retained result; transport loss after possible commit means uncertain outcome until lookup, not rollback. Canonical-only BDP input preferred; optional legacy conversion profile remains a separate decision. Shared admission service beneath CLI/BDP, not looped client create calls.

Please route with the BDP owners: minimum operation/result lookup surface, request/receipt bounds and retention, optional legacy-input profile, and provider transaction/history/receipt seam. These are proposed contracts, not adopted endpoint/schema or implementation/release/runtime scope. Independent local legacy import and priority119 hosted qualification continue unchanged.
